overview.headline: How radioactive decay adds numeric ages to geologic time

keyPoints.point: Earth is about 4.6 billion years old anchors inquiry into numeric age assignment
keyPoints.quote: Earth is about 4.6 billion years old?

keyPoints.point: Half-life length defines time required for parent atoms to decay to daughter atoms
keyPoints.quote: The half-life of a radioactive isotope is the length of time required for exactly one-half of the parent atoms to decay to daughter atoms.

keyPoints.point: Age determinations using radioactive isotopes carry relatively small errors in measurement
keyPoints.quote: Age determinations using radioactive isotopes are subject to relatively small errors in measurement

keyPoints.point: Isotopic techniques measure time when particular mineral within rock formed to support scale ages
keyPoints.quote: Isotopic techniques are used to measure the time at which a particular mineral within a rock was formed.
